title: Just pushed a biome & building variety update to Permit Denied, my browser bulldozer demolition game
author: viral-architect
selftext:
I've been building a browser-based 2.5D bulldozer demolition game called Permit Denied ([https://permitdenied.app/](https://permitdenied.app/)) where you flatten towns across a 63-region US/Canada atlas, run timed challenges or sandbox mode, and upgrade your rig. Getting the initial destruction loop working with AI was fast, but once the codebase grew past prototype size, procedural generation started looking repetitive and geographically wrong—like forests and snow spawning in Arizona, or commercial blocks all sharing the exact same flat roof tiles.

My biggest workflow shift lately has been separating planning from code generation instead of chatting back-and-forth inside the IDE. For this latest update, I fed a full zip of the repo into \[Gemini / my planning model\] first just to audit how map data and building exteriors were wired up, brainstorm missing regional details, and generate a strict single-pass implementation spec before touching a coding agent on a new branch. That let me add desert mesas/boulders, regional landmarks, and rooftop props like HVAC units and restaurant exhaust hoods in one clean pass without breaking existing physics or UI state.

For anyone else maintaining a larger AI-built game rather than starting fresh prototypes: how are you structuring your context and prompts when adding content passes to an existing procedural system? Do you do a separate architecture/spec pass first, or keep everything inside Cursor/CLI agents?
